stories.title: The Field of Panipat — 21 April 1526

scene_setting.moment: Midday — Babur's tulughma curls around Ibrahim Lodi's wings; Ottoman gunners Ustad Ali and Mustafa light the matchlocks; Lodi dies before nightfall.

stories.synopsis: Foundation moment. Gunpowder + flanking divisions decide north India. Babur's foothold becomes the Mughal Empire.

stories.title: The Library Stairs — Delhi, January 1556

scene_setting.moment: Humayun, having just recaptured Delhi the year before, falls down the staircase of his library on hearing the muezzin. Memory tableaux around him: swimming the Ganga at Chausa 1539, exile at Tahmasp's Safavid court, the painters Mir Sayyid Ali and Khwaja Abdus Samad returning with him from Iran.

stories.synopsis: The exile that becomes inheritance. Humayun's fifteen lost years let Sher Shah build the institutional spine (rupiya, GT Road, sarai, zabt prototype) that Akbar will use.

stories.title: Mansab Day — Akbar's Court, c.1580

scene_setting.moment: Todar Mal presents the zabt revenue sheet; mansab ranks are being inscribed for Iranis, Turanis, Afghans, and Rajputs; Raja Man Singh stands at his 7,000-rank station; through the open gate, the stone elephant statues of Jaimal Rathore and Patta Sisodiya — defenders of Chittor — face the court.

stories.synopsis: The composite-nobility machine assembled in one room. Mansabdari + zabt + watan jagirs + subadari operating together; the conquest map (Gujarat→Bengal→Kashmir→Sindh→Berar→Khandesh) is the result.

anchors.label: Raja Man Singh I of Amber

fly_bys.label: Conquest of Bengal & End of Afghan Rule (1574-1576)

stories.title: The Ibadat Khana — Thursday Night, 1578

scene_setting.moment: A Sunni theologian and a Shia theologian argue at volume about the Imamate; a Jain monk from Kathiawar waits his turn; Rodolfo Acquaviva and Antonio Monserrate sit with illustrated Gospels for the emperor; Abu'l Fazl writes in the corner; Birbal sits across; outside the window, Salim Chishti's white tomb glows; in the adjoining courtyard, Mian Tansen tunes for Darbari Kanada.

stories.synopsis: The architecture of synthesis given a single embodied evening. *Sulh-i-kul* is the operating logic; the Mughal painting tradition is being born in the workshop next door; the *Akbarnama* is being drafted in this same hall.

fly_bys.label: First Jesuit Mission to Akbar's Court (1580-1583)

stories.title: Lahore 1606 — The Wound Opens

scene_setting.moment: Guru Arjan is dragged from Lahore Fort and tortured on Jahangir's order; the *Adi Granth* — which he compiled two years earlier at Amritsar — lies open on a table beside him, its pages showing the verses of Kabir, Namdev, Farid, Surdas; a foreground panel shows Hargobind donning two swords (the doctrine of *miri-piri*); a memory tableau within the scene shows Tulsidas at Varanasi finishing the *Ramcharitmanas*, Mirabai singing in Mewar, Dadu Dayal teaching in Rajasthan; Miyan Mir (the Qadariya sufi who laid the Harmandir Sahib's foundation stone) stands at the edge of the scene in grief.

stories.synopsis: The first Mughal-Sikh fracture, framed against the same century's bhakti compilation that the Adi Granth absorbed. The scripture and the martyrdom in one scene.

stories.title: The Chain of Justice — Agra Fort, c.1617

scene_setting.moment: The thirty-yard gold chain hangs from the fort wall to the Yamuna bank, its sixty bells catching the river breeze; Jahangir watches from the jharoka; Nur Jahan inscribes a farman under her own seal at a side desk; Sir Thomas Roe waits in the audience corridor with his East India Company petition; in the open courtyard studio, Ustad Mansur paints a Siberian crane from life; Mirza Ghiyas Beg (Itimad-ud-Daulah) reviews accounts; on the riverbank behind, his own marble tomb is rising under Nur Jahan's commission.

stories.synopsis: Mughal sovereignty presented as personally accountable; a Persian-émigré finance family at the empire's centre; the first English ambassador watching effective power held by a woman.

stories.title: Shahjahanabad, 1656 — The Marble Capital Complete

scene_setting.place: Friday-prayer plaza of the Jama Masjid, Old Delhi
scene_setting.moment: The newly opened Jama Masjid catches Friday light; the planned grid of Shahjahanabad spreads beyond; up the Yamuna at Agra, the Taj Mahal (now thirteen years complete) is visible as a marble glimmer; in the adjacent Diwan-i-Khas of the Red Fort, the Peacock Throne sits beneath the inlaid couplet '*Agar firdaus bar roo-e zameen ast…*'; Abdul Hamid Lahori finalizes a *Badshah Nama* folio on a portable desk in the courtyard; Dara Shukoh walks past with his *Sirr-i-Akbar* manuscript open, Jahanara at his side.

stories.synopsis: Shah Jahan's full vision in a single afternoon — Taj, Peacock Throne, Jama Masjid, Shahjahanabad all complete; the Deccan formally vassal since 1636; Dara's Sufi-Vedanta program present but already vulnerable.

stories.title: Delhi, March 1679 — The Jizya Proclamation

scene_setting.place: Chowk in front of the Red Fort, Delhi
scene_setting.moment: Aurangzeb's *jizya* farman is read out from the Naubat Khana; the Hindu merchants of Delhi sit in a circle blocking the imperial procession; muhtasibs with whips push at the perimeter; François Bernier watches from a balcony, his notebook open showing the half-drafted theory of imperial land ownership; a courtier's desk holds Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi's letters arguing *wahdat-ul-shuhud* against the older Chishti *wahdat-ul-wujud*; the Fatawa-i-Alamgiri compilation team works in a side room; Dara Shukoh's portrait hangs in memorial.

stories.synopsis: The reversal at its most legible moment. Theological policy, juridical compendium, observer's theory of despotism, and the Naqshbandi-over-Chishti doctrinal victory all sit in one square.

stories.title: Aurangabad 1707 — The Empire's Last Camp

scene_setting.moment: Aurangzeb at 88 lies dying in his campaign tent, dictating his final testament; a campaign map showing eight years of Rajaram's hold at Jinji is pinned to the wall; couriers bring news from the Marwar-Mewar front; in a memory panel, Sambhaji is led to his execution at Tulapur 1689; Bibi-ka-Maqbara — the 'poor man's Taj' — rises in the middle distance; Mir Jumla's old shaft-mining gear lies in a corner.

stories.synopsis: Territorial maximum, institutional minimum. Bijapur (1685) and Golconda (1687) fell, but their fall unleashed the Marathas; Aurangzeb is in the Deccan from 1698 onward and will die there.

fly_bys.label: Mirza Raja Jai Singh I of Amber

stories.title: Anandpur, Baisakhi 1699 — The Khalsa Is Born

scene_setting.moment: Guru Gobind Singh under the saffron banner; five volunteers from disparate castes drink amrit from a single iron bowl and emerge as the panj pyaare; the five Ks visible on each; a memory panel within the scene shows Tegh Bahadur's execution at Chandni Chowk in 1675; a forward shadow shows the four sahibzadas' coming deaths (Chamkaur 1705 and the bricking at Sirhind).

stories.synopsis: The Sikh community ceases to be primarily devotional. The Khalsa institution arrives as the direct radicalising response to Aurangzeb's Delhi execution of Tegh Bahadur.

stories.title: Pratapgarh, 10 November 1659 — The Bagh-Nakh

scene_setting.place: Forest-pavilion meeting point below Pratapgarh fort, Western Ghats
scene_setting.moment: Shivaji and Bijapur's general Afzal Khan embrace; the concealed tiger-claw strikes; the Bijapuri retinue is ambushed by Maratha cavalry already deployed in the hills; in a memory panel, Jijabai instructs the young Shivaji in dharma at Poona; his father Shahji Bhonsle's portrait hangs in a corner.

stories.synopsis: Shivaji's signature deed — the moment Mughal contemporaries first recognise him as a sovereign actor, not a raider.

stories.title: Raigarh, 6 June 1674 — Chhatrapati

scene_setting.moment: Shivaji is consecrated *Chhatrapati* by Pandit Gagabhatt; the eight ministers of the Ashtapradhan stand each at their station with their books of office; revenue scrolls inscribed *chauth* and *sardeshmukhi* are laid before the throne; memory tableaux show the 1664 sack of Surat, the Treaty of Purandar 1665, and the 1666 escape from Aurangzeb's Agra court; forward shadows show Sambhaji and the future Peshwas.

stories.synopsis: Maratha state-formation made explicit. The Ashtapradhan + chauth/sardeshmukhi system are not raiding but rational bureaucracy.

stories.title: Ahmadnagar 1595 — Chand Bibi at the Walls

scene_setting.moment: Chand Bibi, regent of Ahmadnagar, in armour on the wall directing the defence against Akbar's besieging army; Malik Ambar — the Ethiopian-born vizier who will pioneer Maratha-cavalry guerrilla warfare — coordinates from horseback; in framed inset panels, Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founds Hyderabad (1591) with the Char Minar at its centre, Ibrahim Adil Shah II composes Dakhini music at Bijapur, and Gol Gumbaz's dome is taking shape; Ibrahim Rauza sits in the same Bijapuri skyline.

stories.synopsis: The Deccan's own synthesis question, running parallel to the Mughal one — multilingual courts, women as effective commanders, African vizier-strategists, an architectural language entirely its own.

fly_bys.label: Ibrahim Adil Shah II of Bijapur

stories.title: Surat Port, October 1670 — The Second Sack

scene_setting.moment: Shivaji's second raid is in progress: customs houses burn; Mughal officials flee; merchants tear hundi paper bills they cannot collect on; bales of *muslin* from Dacca and *chintz* from the Coromandel coast lie split on the quayside; Spanish reales and Mexican 8-real silver coins spill from a money-changer's chest; tomatoes, chillies, and tobacco from American imports sit in a bazaar stall; an English East India Company factor watches from the factory roof.

stories.synopsis: The commercial empire visible at its key port: silver flowing in, cloth flowing out, hundi credit binding it together — and a Maratha raider exposing how thin the imperial military shield over the trade has become.

anchors.label: Global Silver Flow into Mughal India

stories.title: A Bihar Village — Harvest Day, c.1650

scene_setting.place: An open-field Mughal-era village, lower Bihar (suba of Bihar)
scene_setting.moment: The *qanungo* records this year's yield against the zabt-fixed assessment; *khud-kashta* resident peasants and *pahi-kashta* outsiders work different strips of the same field; women in the rear cleaning *jins-i-kamil* cash crops (cotton, indigo, sugarcane); zamindar's agents and the village panchayat negotiate the headman's share at a separate corner; a Persian-wheel irrigation device turns above an open well; a small forest community at the field's edge sells honey and lac.

stories.synopsis: The agrarian engine that finances everything else — Akbar's *zabt* still working, layered with caste, gender, kinship, and the slow shift toward revenue-farming that will become *ijaradari* under decline.

stories.title: The Kitabkhana — A Mughal Studio, c.1700

scene_setting.place: Imperial Kitabkhana, late Mughal Lahore / Delhi; with a side-panel of a Pahari hill studio at Basohli
scene_setting.moment: A master painter finishes a Mughal-style portrait of an Aurangzeb-era noble; in an adjoining panel, a Pahari artist from Basohli works in bold red ground with the new Krishna iconography; further panels: a Kangra atelier under the Katoch rajas in green hills; a Kathak performance in a Rajput courtyard; bound copies of the *Hamzanama* and *Tutinama* on a workshop shelf; Ragamala painting cycles arranged for inspection.

stories.synopsis: The painting tradition Akbar founded has diffused — into Pahari schools, into Rajasthani courts, and into the choreography of court dance. One scene captures the entire post-Akbar visual ecology.

stories.title: Karnal, February 1739 — Nadir Shah's Camp

scene_setting.place: Nadir Shah's tent at Karnal, just after the rout of Muhammad Shah's Mughal army
scene_setting.moment: The Peacock Throne is being loaded onto Persian carts; the Koh-i-Noor changes hands in close-up; in the distance, Delhi burns under the *qatl-e-aam* massacre; a memory panel shows Khafi Khan's 'one pomegranate among a hundred sick' as a caption; Suraj Mal at Bharatpur is sheltering fleeing Mughal nobles in a side-panel; revenue-farming *ijaradari* contracts blow across the camp floor.

stories.synopsis: The structural collapse made spectacular. The jagirdari crisis behind the throne was the deep cause; Nadir's loot is its visible expression.

stories.title: Jaipur 1734 — Sawai Jai Singh at the Jantar Mantar

scene_setting.place: Jantar Mantar observatory courtyard, newly founded city of Jaipur
scene_setting.moment: Sawai Jai Singh II at the great Samrat Yantra sundial; on a stone table beside him, a political map of India c.1734 with five highlighted capitals — Murshidabad (Murshid Quli Khan's Bengal), Lucknow/Faizabad (Saadat Khan's Awadh), Hyderabad (Nizam Asaf Jah), Bharatpur (Suraj Mal's Jat state), Anandpur/Sirhind (the Sikh territories where Banda Bahadur had struck sovereign coins); a Maratha cavalry stream pushes north (Bajirao's expansion) as a background tableau; a smudge on the Bengal coast marks the East India Company's growing factories.

stories.synopsis: The successor states presented as a single moment of pluralising sovereignty — not collapse but reformation. Jaipur the planned city is itself an instance of this new political form.

stories.title: Six Courts, One Hour — Eurasia c.1640

scene_setting.place: Split-screen meta-tableau: six framed windows of one composite illustration
scene_setting.moment: Six contemporaneous courts, all visible at once: (i) Galileo at his telescope in Arcetri (already silenced by the Council of Trent's heirs); (ii) Suleyman's successor era in Istanbul; (iii) Shah Abbas I's Naqsh-i-Jahan square at Isfahan; (iv) the late-Tudor court at Greenwich (Queen Elizabeth's now-historical reign); (v) Tokugawa Iemitsu issuing the *sakoku* seclusion edicts at Edo; (vi) the early-Qing court at Beijing. A village English cricket green and an enclosed field hover at the meta-edge as captions on the era's quiet structural changes.

stories.synopsis: Meta-scene by design (flagged as a bundling-method edge case for convergence): when the cognitive task is 'simultaneity', the embodied-episode test relaxes to split-screen rather than single-stage.
